trust_decision.summary: Which index hits (and how many, via `total`) a user may see from /api/fs/search is decided after the backend query, in the handler: base-path containment plus meta hide/read/password via common.CanAccess. The total is still taken from the unfiltered backend count, and the Bleve backend never scopes hits to req.Parent at all.

landing_point.why: The summary names a path check in Bleve search; Bleve's Search builds its query from keywords and scope only (lines 29-38), ignores req.Parent, and returns the unfiltered searchResults.Total (line 57).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory title says 'Bleve search' and 'path check'; the DB and Meilisearch backends already scope by parent in their own queries (internal/db/searchnode.go:15-22, internal/search/meilisearch/search.go:53-57), so a solver can argue they are not affected. They still leak the count of hidden or password-protected entries, because the handler filters after the total is computed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several behaviours must keep working: correct total and page slicing across pages and across 1000-hit batches with duplicate names; a correct password unlocking results inside protected folders; users who can see hides still seeing hidden entries; descendants of req.Parent (including req.Parent itself) still being returned while sibling-prefix dirs (/base vs /base2) are excluded. Over-broad fixes, such as setting total to the page length, dropping all results in password-protected dirs, or using a raw prefix compare, break these.
